editorial.headline: Briquette Manufacturing With a Scope-Dependent Bali Read
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 19205 covers briquette production from petroleum, coal, peat, or lignite, with national PMA openness but a Bali registration note that depends on the exact declared scope.
editorial.body:
KBLI 19205 is a manufacturing code for briquettes made from petroleum, coal, peat, or lignite. The slim record is deliberately broad: it includes production carried out at the mining site and production done away from it, and it also includes briquettes made from petroleum, coal, peat, or lignite purchased from another party. In plain English, the activity is about turning those fossil or peat-based materials into briquette form, not about a retail channel, an energy-service model, or a neighbouring industrial activity.

The registration scale is equally broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the code is not framed only for heavy industrial operators. It can sit on the books of a smaller manufacturing setup as well as a larger one, provided the registered activity remains exactly within the scope described: making briquettes from petroleum, coal, peat, or lignite, whether the input material is tied to a mining location or bought from outside. That exactness matters because this record’s Bali treatment is not a simple yes-or-no editorial footnote.

Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is clean: the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, with the source listed as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is a foreign-open activity with no lower percentage cap shown in the record. The Bali field, however, is more conditional. It does not mark the code as outright blocked, because l4_bali_blocked is false, but its status is Blocked (scope-dependent). The stated reason is: OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity.

That means the honest Bali reading is not to invent a local percentage cap, a partnership condition, or a separate Bali quota. The record gives none. What it does give is a province-level moratorium rule: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA (island-wide, permanent), with the source listed as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For this code, the practical editorial conclusion is therefore cautious and narrow: nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, but in Bali the PMA registration outcome depends on the exact OSS risk/scope declared, and the record itself says to verify live OSS per exact activity.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this is foreign-open, but the Bali answer turns on the exact OSS risk and scope declared for the activity.
